newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares up, close off high, forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares up, close off high, forecasts.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Wednesday, but eased from the highs towards the close after UES's record-breaking morning climb.
But traders gave conflicting predictions of where the market would head after a long holiday break.
Traders cited healthy consolidated profits reported by UES on Tuesday, a Tuesday Wall Street rise and fears of a liquidity crunch on the market for Wednesday's share price rise.
Many brokers were sure to be away between May 5 and 8, when the market is next open, to take advantage of two long weekends in Russia, traders said.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index rose five percent to 321.19 from Tuesday's 305.53.
Unified Energy System finished at $0.2600, off a high close to 27 cents but up from Tuesday's $0.2380. LUKoil rose to $14.20 from $13.85.
Market volume was a healthy $41.6 million though seen high on pre-holiday buying. Russian markets will be closed for May holidays on May 1-4 and 9-11.

CentreInvest Strategic Investment Director Alexander Babian said the market would rise five to eight percent in the next two weeks as experienced investors in Russia placed new funds, especially in local telecoms and undervalued leading shares with American Depositary Receipts programmes allowing trading abroad.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell head trader Pavel Gronbjerg said Wall Street would probably slip on U.S. first quarter GDP figures showing a 5.6 percent annualised growth rate, which some investors fear could indicate an overheating economy and cause the U.S. Federal Reserve to hike interests rates.
But he declined to predict next week's trend.
Another Western trader said the market would be flat.
